subject.title: iPhone Continuity Camera `--facing front` always uses rear camera

question: Should macOS camera capture treat `--facing front|back` as a secondary lens selector when an explicit iPhone Continuity Camera `--device-id` is also supplied?
rationale: Current source treats `deviceId` as an exact camera selector before front/back lookup, while the requested behavior would make `facing` affect a selected external device; that precedence contract needs maintainer intent plus live AVFoundation proof.

options.title: Preserve exact device targeting
options.body: Keep `deviceId` as the highest-precedence selector and add a clear limitation or diagnostic if Continuity Camera exposes only one selectable external camera.

options.title: Add Continuity lens selection
options.body: If live proof shows AVFoundation exposes a reliable front/back selector for the same iPhone, add a narrow macOS implementation and coverage for that behavior.

options.title: Let facing override device id
options.body: Allow `facing` to replace or ignore an explicit `deviceId`, accepting compatibility risk for multi-camera users who expect exact device targeting.

recommendation.title: Preserve exact device targeting
recommendation.body: Keep `deviceId` as the highest-precedence selector and add a clear limitation or diagnostic if Continuity Camera exposes only one selectable external camera.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-history owner for the macOS camera picker and prior device-id support discussion.
